title: Lean runtime ops weekly outline (Lina) - scratchpad
content:
Purpose: quick, focused prep for the combined runtime + infra + console weekly. Keep it lean (45m). This is my scratchpad — action items and owners are tentative.

Meeting basics (45m):
- Facilitator: Lina Duarte (start on time)
- Attendees: runtime leads + infra oncall + console PM + SRE rep (Marco / Ethan / Priya / Anya)
- Timebox: 10m updates / 25m deep focus / 10m action-review + parking lot

Goals for this week:
1) Blocker triage: unblock the canary regressions seen on 3/9 (p95 spike during bursts).
2) Decide whether to flip the KV cache size bump for dedicated pools (rollout plan + rollback).
3) Surface one console UX iteration to reduce operator confusion on route fallbacks.

Quick status (each person 1 min):
- Runtime: p50 stable, p95 +18% vs last week under burst traffic; reproduction on smaller seq len.
- Infra: one node pool update delayed (driver upgrade), ETA 3/17.
- Console: rollout for route diagnostics delayed, need final backend hook.

Data slices to have ready (priors):
- p50/p95/p99 token latency last 72h (split hosted vs dedicated)
- GPU util by instance type, 1h/6h/24h windows
- Error rate by model variant since 3/1 (notes on any correlation with kernel changes)

Focus topic A (15m): p95 spikes during synthetic-burst test
- Symptoms: sustained p95 spikes for 30-90s when concurrent short requests jump ~3x.
- Hypothesis 1: scheduler/continuous-batch boundary inefficient for short sequences => queue serialization.
- Hypothesis 2: KV cache misses trigger slower path; particular for quantized variants.
- Prep: Marco to bring a short log extract (tail) + one full request timeline for a sample burst.
- Decision needed: temporary mitigation (increase batching threshold OR preferentially route short seq to low-latency pool).

Focus topic B (6m): KV cache size bump for Dedicated pools (proposal review)
- Proposed change: increase per-worker prefix cache from 256KB to 768KB for gpu-t4x workers (ENG-2345).
- Benefits: reduced repeated token recompute for mid-length prompts observed in commerce flows.
- Risks: extra memory pressure, potential OOM on older drivers.
- Rollout suggestion: stage to canary pool (10% traffic) + retention 24h, auto-fallback on >1.5x error or memory event.
- Decision: vote in meeting — need a thumbs up / concerns recorded.

Focus topic C (4m): Console route diagnostics UX quick win
- Problem: operators open route detail and can't easily tell which fallback model served the request.
- Ask: console PM to show simple model lineage + last-fallback-at timestamp on top of route detail.
- Quick mock: Priya has 1 slide; show it and get alignment.

Action item review and owners (end of meeting, confirm live):
- AI-1: Marco - attach the 3 burst logs and highlight candidate request ids (due 2026-03-13).
- AI-2: Ethan - run small canary with KV cache bump on staging, report memory stats (due 2026-03-14).
- AI-3: Priya - update console mock and add quick copy for fallback timestamp (due 2026-03-15).
- AI-4: Lina - draft rollback checklist for cache bump (include metrics thresholds + who calls rollback) (due 2026-03-14).
- AI-5: Anya (SRE) - prepare node-pool upgrade contingency plan if driver upgrade conflicts with canary (due 2026-03-16).

Parking lot / follow-ups (post-meeting):
- Investigate scheduler-level instrumentation for sub-50ms queuing events (might need small runtime probe).
- Align with Optimize team about batching suggestions for short-seq heavy tenants.

Prep checklist (what I need before the sync):
- Pull p95/p99 charts and annotate suspected time windows (Lina)
- Confirm Marco will share raw logs and a sanitized request id sample
- Slack ping Priya to make sure the mock is in the slide deck by EOD day-before
- Open quick PR template for rollback checklist (so we can iterate in meeting)

Notes to self / rough script:
- Start with quick wins: show p95 trend + spike window (get buy-in this is real).
- Move to mitigation options: low-effort mitigations first (routing tweak) then cache bump.
- If cache bump chosen, confirm canary size + explicit fallback thresholds before leaving meeting.

Open questions I want answer to in the meeting:
- Are the p95 spikes limited to a handful of tenants or widespread?
- Does kernel selector log suggest a hot-path change correlating with the spike times?
- Can we replicate locally with the modified batching threshold?

Tone & meeting rules:
- Keep it crisp; call out blockers and owners. If topic needs >15m, table for a deep-dive follow-up.
- Avoid design-by-committee; capture dissent and next steps.

Revision log (this doc):
- 2026-03-10: initial outline and goals (Lina)
- 2026-03-12: added action-item owners + linked artifacts

Random reminders (notes-to-self):
- If Marco is out, fallback: get logs from infra-logs-s3 bucket (path in confluence page).
- Remember to ask PM about telemetry retention window for route diagnostics (we might need 30d).

-- end of scratchpad --
